scenes.caption: Green coffee doesn't taste like coffee. Roasting is where the flavor gets made.
Raw beans are hard and pale, and they smell like hay.
First the heat drives out moisture. The beans go from green to yellow.
Then the browning starts. This is where the coffee smell shows up.
Around 385°F the beans pop. Like popcorn, only quieter. Light roasts finish near here.
Push on to about 435°F and they crack again. Oils reach the surface. That's dark roast.

scenes.text: More time in the drum, darker bean
scenes.caption: Time and heat set the color. Color tells you a lot about the cup.
Light tastes bright and fruity. Dark tastes bold and smoky. Neither one is better.

scenes.sub: Cool fast to stop the roast. Rest a day or two.
scenes.caption: Cool them fast to stop the roast. Then let them rest a day or two.
